posts.cooked: One thing I really really really appreciate about Sentinels is that there's little appreciable difference between the names given to male characters and female characters. Several characters do have names that identify or imply gender, but it's not the rule.

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
Gendered names... Let's see...

On the villain side we have Baron Blade, The Matriarch, The Chairman (although given the "hides in the shadows" character type, I could totally see a woman being the "Chairman"), Man-Grove (not that Man-Grove really has a gender), Magman, and Miss Information.  I'm not counting the Ennead, even though you could figure out their genders if you're familiar with the gods that they are inspired by, or Calypso (or Ra) because those are names rather than titles.

 

On the hero side we have Mr. Fixer, Stuntman, and La Comodora.  You could make a case for The Harpy as well, although the sexism there is more a little less direct.

 

That's 9 or 10 characters in total out of at least 100.  I am slightly amused that Lillian appears on the list twice.

posts.name: Ironic
posts.cooked:
Belle Sorciere:

I love seeing it. Previously I'd primarily seen this sort of naming in the X-Men and among City of Heroes players.

It's more or less become the standard for new characters across the past few decades - look at the Teen Titans OCs (Raven, Cyborg, and Starfire), or the members of Youngbloods (a pretty awful comic for gender equality in general, but I'll admit that I couldn't tell you based on names alone which of Chapel, Masada, Riptide and Photon are women*), or a bunch of other characters of more recent vintage.  The Legion of Superheroes even gave up their absurd "boy" "girl" and "lass/lad" style names in favor of classier stuff like "Umbra" and "Polestar" for a while.

But, certainly, it was X-Men that set the tone and led to that becoming the norm - and it's chiefly in X-Men where characters in that style are the majority of famous and respected icons, rather than C-listers.  That's part of what makes it so sweet to see that convention picked up in Sentinels.

 

  • It's Riptide and Masada.  Yes, like that laser gun that Chrono-Ranger uses.  See, she's Jewish, and that's the name of a fortress near Jerusalem.  You know, because Con was created by (and acts like) Unity - now confirmed!
